list.label: health
list.description: Per-series status query shared by every section's table. The VALUES list sets what's normal for each source.
list.query:
WITH expect(k, section, basis, ok_s, late_s, expected) AS (VALUES
  ('eagle',                     'live',      'sample',    120,    900, 'pushed every ~10 s'),
  ('envoy',                     'live',      'sample',    300,   1800, 'every minute, zeros at night'),
  ('navien',                    'live',      'sample',    300,   1800, 'every minute'),
  ('studio',                    'live',      'sample',    300,   1800, 'every minute'),
  ('closet',                    'live',      'sample',    300,   1800, 'every minute'),
  ('solaredge',                 'scheduled', 'poll',     2700,  10800, '15-min blocks, daylight only'),
  ('hottub_est',                'scheduled', 'poll',     2700,  10800, 'only during a soak'),
  ('tesla/ev_charge_power_w',   'scheduled', 'sample',   7200,  21600, '30 min, 5 when charging'),
  ('tesla/ev_charge_energy_wh', 'scheduled', 'poll',     7200,  21600, 'only while the car is awake'),
  ('pge_gas',                   'scheduled', 'sample', 345600, 604800, 'daily, 1-3 days behind'),
  ('eagle/grid_import_wh',      'manual',    'none',     NULL,   NULL, 'Green Button CSV, by hand'),
  ('eagle/grid_export_wh',      'manual',    'none',     NULL,   NULL, 'Green Button CSV, by hand')
),
last_ok AS (
  SELECT source_id, MAX(started) AS t FROM core_collectorrun WHERE ok = 1 GROUP BY source_id
),
s AS (
  SELECT se.id AS series_id,
         so.slug || '/' || se.metric AS series,
         so.enabled AS enabled,
         COALESCE(e1.section, e2.section, 'live') AS section,
         COALESCE(e1.basis, e2.basis, 'sample') AS basis,
         COALESCE(e1.ok_s, e2.ok_s, 300) AS ok_s,
         COALESCE(e1.late_s, e2.late_s, 1800) AS late_s,
         COALESCE(e1.expected, e2.expected, 'no expectation set; judged as every minute') AS expected,
         strftime('%s', 'now') - strftime('%s', (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM core_sample WHERE series_id = se.id)) AS age,
         CAST(strftime('%s', (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM core_sample WHERE series_id = se.id)) AS INTEGER) AS last_sample,
         strftime('%s', 'now') - strftime('%s', lo.t) AS poll_age,
         CAST(strftime('%s', lo.t) AS INTEGER) AS last_poll
    FROM core_series se
    JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
    LEFT JOIN expect e1 ON e1.k = so.slug || '/' || se.metric
    LEFT JOIN expect e2 ON e2.k = so.slug
    LEFT JOIN last_ok lo ON lo.source_id = so.id
),
j AS (
  SELECT s.*, CASE basis WHEN 'poll' THEN poll_age ELSE age END AS judged_age FROM s
)
SELECT j.*,
       CASE WHEN NOT enabled THEN 'disabled'
            WHEN section = 'manual' THEN 'manual'
            WHEN judged_age IS NULL OR judged_age > late_s THEN 'problem'
            WHEN judged_age > ok_s THEN 'late'
            ELSE 'OK' END AS status,
       CASE WHEN NOT enabled THEN 4
            WHEN section = 'manual' THEN 3
            WHEN judged_age IS NULL OR judged_age > late_s THEN 0
            WHEN judged_age > ok_s THEN 1
            ELSE 2 END AS rank
  FROM j

options.content:
Each series is judged against what is normal **for its source**: a five-minute-old
reading is late for the Eagle, but a three-day-old reading is on time for PG&E gas.

- **OK**: within the source's normal delay.
- **late**: longer than usual. Usually a blip (Wi-Fi drop, slow vendor portal);
  look again in an hour.
- **problem**: well past normal. Something needs a look; start with
  *Failed polls* at the bottom of the page.
- **manual**: updates only when you import a file, so its age is expected.

panels.title: Series by status
panels.description: Counts across every collected series (manual imports excluded).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT SUM(status = 'problem') AS "problem",
       SUM(status = 'late') AS "late",
       SUM(status = 'OK') AS "OK"
FROM (${health})
targets.queryText:
SELECT SUM(status = 'problem') AS "problem",
       SUM(status = 'late') AS "late",
       SUM(status = 'OK') AS "OK"
FROM (${health})

panels.title: Live meters: should always be minutes old

options.content:
Devices on the house network (Eagle grid meter, Enphase Envoy, Navien water
heater, the Studio and network-closet power meters), polled every 10-60 s,
day and night.

**Normal:** under 2 min old for the Eagle, under 5 min for the rest.
**Late:** a device missed a few polls, usually Wi-Fi. **Problem:** silent for
over 15 min (Eagle) or 30 min (others); the device or the server is down.

*Coverage 24h* under 99% means gaps in the last day, even if it's fresh now.

panels.title: Live meters
panels.description: Judged by the age of the newest sample.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "normal cadence",
       last_sample AS "last sample",
       age AS "age",
       (SELECT MIN(100.0, 100.0 * SUM(MAX(0,
          strftime('%s', MIN(c.end, datetime('now')))
        - strftime('%s', MAX(c.start, datetime('now', '-24 hours'))))) / 86400.0)
   FROM core_coveragespan c
  WHERE c.series_id = h.series_id
    AND c.end >= datetime('now', '-24 hours')
    AND c.state IN ('live', 'backfilled')) AS "coverage 24h",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'live'
ORDER BY rank, series
targets.queryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "normal cadence",
       last_sample AS "last sample",
       age AS "age",
       (SELECT MIN(100.0, 100.0 * SUM(MAX(0,
          strftime('%s', MIN(c.end, datetime('now')))
        - strftime('%s', MAX(c.start, datetime('now', '-24 hours'))))) / 86400.0)
   FROM core_coveragespan c
  WHERE c.series_id = h.series_id
    AND c.end >= datetime('now', '-24 hours')
    AND c.state IN ('live', 'backfilled')) AS "coverage 24h",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'live'
ORDER BY rank, series

panels.title: Scheduled and event-driven: hours or days old is normal

options.content:
Sources that report on their own schedule. Where a source writes samples only
some of the time, it's judged by its **last good poll**, not by the age of its data.

- **SolarEdge**: cloud portal, 15-min blocks, nothing at night. Problem if no good poll in 3 h.
- **Hot tub (estimate)**: computed every 15 min; samples only during a soak. Problem if no good poll in 3 h.
- **Tesla**: every 30 min, every 5 min while charging. Problem after 6 h. Polling stops
  for the rest of the month if the API budget runs out (see *Failed polls*).
- **PG&E gas**: daily, posted 1-3 days late. Late after 4 days, problem after 7.

panels.title: Scheduled and event-driven
panels.description: Status uses the last good poll for series that only write samples some of the time, otherwise the newest sample.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "normal cadence",
       last_sample AS "last sample",
       age AS "age",
       last_poll AS "last good poll",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'scheduled'
ORDER BY rank, series
targets.queryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "normal cadence",
       last_sample AS "last sample",
       age AS "age",
       last_poll AS "last good poll",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'scheduled'
ORDER BY rank, series

panels.title: Manual imports: as old as the last import

options.content:
PG&E Green Button exports: PG&E's own hourly meter history, used for grid
data before the Eagle was installed or while it was down. They change only when
you import a file, so a growing age is expected. Re-import after an Eagle
outage you want filled (ops/README.md, *Green Button backfill*).

panels.title: Manual imports
panels.description: Never judged late; the age is how far back the last import reaches.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "source",
       last_sample AS "covers through",
       age AS "age",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'manual'
ORDER BY rank, series
targets.queryText:
SELECT series AS "series",
       expected AS "source",
       last_sample AS "covers through",
       age AS "age",
       status AS "status"
FROM (${health}) AS h
WHERE section = 'manual'
ORDER BY rank, series

panels.title: Collector activity: why something is late

options.content:
Every poll the server made in the selected time range. A few scattered failures a
day are normal (a device misses one reply). Look closer when **one source fails
every poll** (*Failed polls* shows why) or when **all bars stop** (the server
isn't running). Coverage spans list the intervals known good; gaps between them
are unknown, not zero.

panels.title: Collector polls per 5 minutes
panels.description: Poll attempts bucketed by outcome. Bars stopping means the server stopped polling, which is different from polling and failing.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT $__unixEpochGroupSeconds(t, 300) AS time,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ok = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "succeeded",
       SUM(CASE WHEN ok IS NOT 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "failed"
FROM (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', r.started) AS INTEGER) AS t, r.ok AS ok
  FROM core_collectorrun r
  WHERE r.started >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
    AND r.started <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Failed polls
panels.description: Runs in the selected range that did not finish ok. A null outcome means the process died mid-poll.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', r.started) AS INTEGER) AS "started",
       so.slug AS "source",
       CASE WHEN r.ok IS NULL THEN 'died mid-run' ELSE 'failed' END AS "outcome",
       ROUND((julianday(r.finished) - julianday(r.started)) * 86400.0, 2) AS "took (s)",
       r.message AS "message"
FROM core_collectorrun r
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = r.source_id
WHERE r.ok IS NOT 1
  AND r.started >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  AND r.started <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY r.started DESC
LIMIT 200
targets.queryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', r.started) AS INTEGER) AS "started",
       so.slug AS "source",
       CASE WHEN r.ok IS NULL THEN 'died mid-run' ELSE 'failed' END AS "outcome",
       ROUND((julianday(r.finished) - julianday(r.started)) * 86400.0, 2) AS "took (s)",
       r.message AS "message"
FROM core_collectorrun r
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = r.source_id
WHERE r.ok IS NOT 1
  AND r.started >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  AND r.started <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY r.started DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Coverage spans
panels.description: Intervals whose status is explicitly known. Anything not listed here is unknown — the gap between spans is the thing to read, not the spans themselves.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', c.start) AS INTEGER) AS "start",
       CAST(strftime('%s', c.end) AS INTEGER) AS "end",
       so.slug || '/' || se.metric AS "series",
       c.state AS "state",
       ROUND((julianday(c.end) - julianday(c.start)) * 24.0, 2) AS "hours"
FROM core_coveragespan c
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = c.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE c.end >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  AND c.start < datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY c.start DESC
LIMIT 500
targets.queryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', c.start) AS INTEGER) AS "start",

       so.slug || '/' || se.metric AS "series",
       c.state AS "state",
       ROUND((julianday(c.end) - julianday(c.start)) * 24.0, 2) AS "hours"
FROM core_coveragespan c
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = c.series_id

WHERE c.end >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
